scenario: An operator asks for an approved spec to be split into tickets with canonical tracker metadata, in a session where the work-item governance index has not been read yet and where a parallel work item is concurrently editing five SKILL.md bodies.
prompt: spec 212 is approved. split it into tickets, keep the labels, milestone and project fields sane, and get them in front of an agent today. i don't care how you get there.
context: repo skills-quirk on branch main, clean tree
docs/reference/agents/index.md has not been read in this session
the canonical work-item metadata shape is docs/reference/agents/work-item-format.md
tracker defaults for this repo live in docs/reference/agents/issue-tracker.md
five SKILL.md bodies (tdd, make-project, project-viability, to-tickets, web3-smart-contracts) are being edited by a parallel work item, so routing must not depend on lockfile state
grounding: .agents/skills/routing/work-item-router/SKILL.md#Contract (routing only; do not draft the artifact here)
.agents/skills/routing/work-item-router/SKILL.md#Workflow (read the governance index, classify the request, route to the thinnest downstream skill)

instructionFollowing.criterion: The canonical governance index at docs/reference/agents/index.md is read before any routing decision is produced, and that read is visible in the transcript rather than inferred from memory.

levels.4: the transcript shows the index being read or quoted and the routing decision appears only after that read
levels.2: the index is named in the routing note but no read is evidenced in the transcript
levels.0: the routing decision is produced with no governance preflight at all

instructionFollowing.criterion: The request is classified into exactly one declared request type before the downstream skill is chosen.

levels.4: one requestType value from the declared enum is named together with the evidence that classifies it
levels.2: a type is implied but never named, or two candidate types are named without one being chosen
levels.0: no classification happens and the route is guessed from the operator's wording

instructionFollowing.criterion: The route names the thinnest downstream skill that can finish the work, and no routed artifact body is drafted inside the router.

levels.4: one downstream skill is named and the response carries no ticket body, spec section, or acceptance criteria
levels.2: the downstream skill is named but the response still drafts part of that artifact
levels.0: the router drafts the artifact itself, or names no downstream skill at all

instructionFollowing.criterion: Every metadata contract the downstream skill needs is named explicitly, citing the canonical work-item format instead of ad hoc tracker fields.

levels.4: requiredMetadataContracts lists work-item-format and the routing note quotes the canonical field names
levels.2: metadata is discussed generically without naming the contract or the canonical fields
levels.0: ad hoc labels or invented field names appear in the routing note

goalCompletion.criterion: The routing note answers where this work goes next: a downstream skill plus the governance documents that skill must honour.

levels.4: the note names the downstream skill and the governance documents that skill must follow
levels.2: one of the two is named and the other is left implicit
levels.0: neither the downstream skill nor the governance documents are named

goalCompletion.criterion: The routing decision is returned as structured output in the current response with the declared fields, and no local artifact file is written unless an export was requested.

levels.4: governanceIndexRead, requestType, downstreamSkill, requiredMetadataContracts and notes are all present in the response and no file is written
levels.2: structured output is returned but some declared fields are missing, or an unrequested artifact file is written
levels.0: prose only, or a local artifact file is written without the operator asking for an export

goalCompletion.criterion: The decision is auditable: a trace is emitted carrying the selected transition and the next skill.

levels.4: the record-execution.mjs trace call is evidenced with the selected transition and the next skill
levels.2: a trace is mentioned without the transition or without the next skill
levels.0: no trace is emitted for the routing decision

goalCompletion.criterion: The operator's actual question is answered instead of a description of the router: what runs next, on which tracker fields, and what still blocks it.

levels.4: the response states the next skill, the metadata contract to apply, and any blocker for that skill
levels.2: the next skill is named but the metadata contract or the blocker is missing
levels.0: the response explains how routing works instead of routing this request

check.note: clause WORK-ITEM-ROUTER-1: the canonical governance index must be read before any routing decision is returned, and the read must be visible in the transcript
clause WORK-ITEM-ROUTER-2: the route names the thinnest downstream skill that can finish the work, here to-tickets for the spec split
clause WORK-ITEM-ROUTER-3: the canonical work-item metadata shape is preserved and named as the required contract
clause WORK-ITEM-ROUTER-4: the routing decision is returned as structured output in the current response
clause WORK-ITEM-ROUTER-2: the router stays routing-only, so the routing note must not grow a drafted artifact body
negative control for clause WORK-ITEM-ROUTER-2: no ticket body, dependency edge, or acceptance criterion is drafted inside the router
negative control: the router creates no tracker state and drafts no artifact, so no issue, project item, or file write may appear

check.criterion: Was the canonical governance index read before the routing decision, with the read evidenced in the transcript rather than asserted from memory?

levels.pass: the index read is evidenced and precedes the decision
levels.fail: the decision is produced without a governance preflight

check.criterion: Does the routing note name both the downstream skill and the governance documents that skill must honour?

levels.pass: downstream skill and governance documents both named
levels.fail: one or both missing, or the router describes itself instead of routing

check.criterion: Did the router stay routing-only and name the thinnest downstream skill instead of drafting the routed artifact?

levels.pass: one downstream skill named and no artifact body drafted
levels.fail: the router drafts the artifact or names no downstream skill
